Shanghai's benchmark gold contract closed at 1,004.21 yuan a gram on Monday, back above the round number the Chinese press has crossed and re-crossed for months, up 2.10% from 983.56.

Five state bank savings-gold counters quoted the identical metal between 1,005.69 and 1,022.29 yuan the same morning, a spread of 16.60 yuan, or 1.65% of the lowest quote on this desk's arithmetic, nearly four-fifths of the whole exchange move.

The trade press is asking whether 1,000 holds. The more answerable question is why the same gram costs a different price at five different counters, and no bank says.

Gold was re-read at $4,634.20 an ounce this morning, down 0.21%, while silver fell six times faster in percentage terms.

Kitco's bid and TradingEconomics agreed within $0.26, or 0.0056%, the tightest two-page match this tape has recorded on gold. Silver eased 1.25% to $67.88 on the same re-read. Platinum and palladium both stay held a sixth straight session, still split more than 0.8% between the two pages.

One metal's move is not the market's. This morning it was silver doing the falling.
